title: Someone Else's Light
premise: A window lit in the small hours, and whoever left it on.

stages.narration: Four floors up, one window is lit — a steady, ordinary yellow, the colour of a room with someone in it. No signal, no message, nothing meant for you. Just a light somebody decided was worth the risk tonight.

choices.label: Mark the building — someone is holding out here
A light is a thing that draws them. Keep moving

notes: T60 · the measured counterweight to `the-small-hours`. The toned ambient pool had four relief scenes and not one was eligible at night: birdsong is dawn/morning, tending-the-base needs a shelter, across-the-street and the-stray are node-kind gated. Meanwhile the-small-hours is a TENSION scene gated on stress, so it becomes eligible exactly when the player is in trouble — i.e. exactly when the director is asking for relief. Measured (`measure/t60.ts --lean`, table (c)), the relief beat has the pool's FEWEST relief-toned rows eligible, 0.72 against its 1.36 tension rows. A lean can only choose between eligible rows, so no multiplier fixes that; only content can. Deliberately un-gated on need or stress and available in every node kind, because the point is that it is there when nothing else is. Same shape as birdsong (sit / mark / press on) so the relief is priced the same. It did NOT close the gap on its own — post-fix the relief beat still delivers slightly more tension than a hold turn does — and that is PL-M5-83, not a claim made here.
